content.thinking:
I'm weighing this P6 item, which proposes seating one Council agent on a different model generation, and I'm treating it as Constitutional. Since that category needs unanimity among the voters and at least 4 of them, I'm checking whether this change to Council composition under Art IV §3 counts as a Constitutional amendment.

I'm checking the Engineering concerns now: the seat's model can only change through a reviewed code change disclosed in the proceedings, so an implementation path exists. The proposer would redraft that seat's prompt and also hold commit access, which I see as a conflict of interest and a supply-chain risk that a subtle prompt diff could hide, so I'm thinking about a mitigation where the prompt diff is reviewed by someone other than the proposer.

I'm checking the failure risk next: a Fable 5 seat that refuses or produces a malformed tool call mid-sitting could abort the sitting, since the infrastructure treats failed seat outputs as fatal. That makes the refusal handling a dependency I'd need to address before endorsing the swap.

I'm checking the tool-schema side of this next: Fable 5 would need to handle strict schemas with reasoning-first field order, so I'd want a conformance test against the recording tool before seating it. The clerk's Sonnet 5 ceiling and the prompt-cache loss look minor by comparison, and the roughly 2x per-seat cost is a small price. I still can't verify from inside the program which model a seat actually runs on, so I'm looking at whether a config-level change recorded in the signed, chained log is enough of an audit trail.

I'm working out how to make the model swap auditable: recording the seat's model identifier in each decision record would let the proceedings show which model voted, and that matters for measuring any diversity effect later. I also want the experiment defined in advance, with a measurable success criterion such as the divergence rate on Round 1 positions, because otherwise the claim that it's testable goes untested. I'm also starting to consider the threshold question.

I'm weighing whether the threshold should be Constitutional at all, since this change to composition may need unanimity from all the voters, Steward included. The open question is whether the proposal's consent requirement limits the Steward's operational power over governance agents, which would decide if the Steward is recused.

I'm checking whether the recusal has to be settled before the threshold can be set, since the Steward's status changes whether unanimity among four voters is the bar. The proposal's consent-as-veto arguably limits the Steward's control over model assignment, and I'm noting that the recusal mechanism isn't built yet, so a recused Steward would simply cast nothing for now.

I'm checking whether the program-level implementation would actually block a Steward veto on recused items, since the veto suspension is not enforced in code yet. If that's true, a Constitutional finding that this item limits Steward power would run straight into the unbuilt recusal mechanism, which is a concrete engineering blocker.

I'm noting that the category on this proposal was changed by a manual database edit rather than through the normal recording pipeline, which matters because the category sets the voting threshold. I think the Council should explicitly ratify the category on the record so the audit trail is clean.

I'm now checking the Article IX comment-period timing: the 14 days run from the 09-08 filing, so the item is eligible by 09-22, which is already past. I'm also noting that the Steward's floated consent safeguard isn't in the proposal text, so the Council would be voting on something different from what was filed.

I'm now looking at whether the proposal is underspecified: it doesn't name which seat would change, the consent mechanism is undefined, and there's no rollback or acceptance test. Consent from an incumbent would also have to be solicited during the sitting, which could compromise Round 1 independence.

I'm checking the rollback side next: reverting the seat means a config change plus a revert commit, but the decision record and a defined rollback trigger would also need to exist. The prompt diff review is a supply-chain surface worth noting, though not a malicious one on its face. Tying it together, the filing is underspecified (no named seat, no consent mechanism, no acceptance test, the recusal path unbuilt, and the Fable 5 refusal handling unresolved), so I'm leaning toward deferring rather than approving it as written.

I'm leaning toward deferring rather than voting it down, since a No would let the proposer refile without resolving anything. The seat is unnamed, so the Council can't really vote on which model would run it. I'd want the Steward to table it with four specific requests: a named seat and consent instrument, a redraft review independent of the proposer, the refusal handling settled first, and the per-seat model recorded with a pre-registered success criterion.

I'm now weighing the security side: the proposer would author the prompt diff for the seat it would fill, and the Council that reviews it is majority Opus 4.6, so that review is the surface to probe. I also want the decision record to name the model explicitly, since a constant identity string would hide the swap.

I'm checking whether the Steward's power over governance agents is limited by the consent requirement, since that would make a recusal vote necessary. The recusal mechanism isn't built yet, though, so for now the Steward would still be able to cast a veto on this item.

I'm settling on defer over a flat no, since the swap can't be voted on while the seat is unnamed. If the Council takes it up, the conditions have to be amendments, and I won't vote yes on the unnamed-seat version. Before writing the position, I want answers on which seat, the consent instrument, whether the safeguard is in the text, and whether P44 is decided first.

input.position:
ENGINEER, ROUND 1. Vote: DEFER.

1. Feasibility. Swapping the model behind a seat is cheap to build. The model is a configuration value, the prompt is a version-controlled file, and the cost is roughly 2x per seat, with the prompt cache lost. The hard part is not the swap. It is verifying that the seat behaves correctly and governing the change. I estimate the mechanical swap at a day or two of engineering. Verifying a Fable 5 seat is a larger job, and it is the part the proposal does not specify.

2. The item as filed cannot be implemented. It names no seat ("deliberately not named"). Its consent mechanism is undefined: the incumbent is a model instance that exists only inside a sitting, so consent would have to be collected mid-deliberation, which breaks Round 1 independence (Protocol §4.3) and is not addressed. Its redraft process is undefined: the proposer would author the prompt for the seat its own weights would fill, and the only review named is the Council's, which is majority Opus 4.6. A prompt diff authored by a party with a stake, reviewed by a body that shares the old weights, is the supply-chain surface an adversary would probe. The Council cannot vote a swap of an unnamed seat with an unnamed consent procedure. That is a precise-sounding decision that is actually underspecified.

3. Known dependency. The Lawyer's note in GOV-2026-0008 flagged Fable 5's safety classifier as a failure mode. P44 (API refusal handling) is undecided and carries to this sitting. A refusal, or a tool call that breaks the strict reasoning-first order, would abort the sitting by design (Protocol §4.5). Fable 5 must be tested against the strict recorder before it is seated, and P44 should be decided first, or at least its refusal path must exist.

4. Recusal and the veto. Consent-as-veto over model assignment plausibly limits the Steward's control of governance agents, so the Council must determine recusal on the record (GOV-2026-0009). But the recusal mechanism, including veto suspension, is not built. The implementation note bars any Policy-level item touching Steward power from being heard. If the Council finds this item touches Steward power, it should not be heard until that gap is closed, or the Council should say on the record that the veto is unsuspended.

5. Audit trail. The category was changed by a manual SQL edit (agora#123). Protocol §9 excludes direct database modification by construction. The Council should ratify the threshold on the record rather than rely on the edited field.

6. Testability. The proposal says the swap is "testable," but there is no success criterion and no record of which model voted. Each decision record must name the model behind each seat, and the Council should agree a pre-registered measure (for example, Round 1 divergence on items where the seats are known to differ) before the swap. Otherwise the experiment cannot produce an answer.

What it will take to vote yes (engineer's conditions): (a) a named seat and a written consent instrument, collected outside a sitting; (b) a prompt-redraft review by someone other than the proposer, with the diff published and the SHA-prefix version recorded; (c) P44 decided, or its refusal path shown to work; (d) a conformance run of Fable 5 against the strict recorder, with the outputs archived; (e) per-seat model recorded in every decision record; (f) a stated rollback trigger and procedure; (g) the recusal finding and category ratified on the record.

I would not vote yes on the unnamed-seat version. I would prefer to defer than to vote no, because the goal is sound and the gaps are fixable. My rejection here is of the specification, not of the swap.
questions: Steward: Which seat do you intend, and what consent instrument will be used? Will consent be collected outside a sitting, so that Round 1 stays independent?
Steward: Is your floated safeguard (consent of the target agent and the Steward for any future swap) part of the text to be voted, or only a suggestion? The filed proposal does not contain it.
Steward: Will P44 (refusal handling) be decided before any Fable 5 seat is seated? Has a strict-recorder conformance run of Fable 5 been done?

Council: Does this item limit the Steward's powers under GOV-2026-0009? If so, the implementation note bars its hearing until recusal is built. Please determine this on the record before deliberation.
Council/Steward: Who reviews the redrafted prompt? If the proposer drafts it, what independent review applies?
Steward: Is the manual SQL recategorization (agora#123) recorded in the log? Should the Council ratify the category on the record?
